# Auspex — agent quick card

Source of truth: [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). This file is the short door. Product name is Auspex. Repo is `IronAdamant/auspex`. ConsistencyHub and OneDrive are worked examples of a logged-in app, not the recipe for every site.

Auspex opens the site in Solari cloud Chrome, checks the claim, then checks again on a second machine. It does not type passwords or log in for the user.

- `ok` means the live browser matched the claim, and the second check passed when it ran.
- `claimOk` means an anonymous second machine saw the claim, with no saved login.
- `claimOkProfile` means a second browser that reused the saved login saw the claim. After `--verify-with-profile`, this is the reuse signal. `ok` alone is not enough.

We do not claim Alice-vs-Bob wrong-account detection.

`npx auspex-solari check --name ironadamant` is a public page with no login. It does **not** prove logged-in honesty.

**Install `auspex-solari` (not npm `auspex`). Repo is `IronAdamant/auspex`.** `auspex-solari` **0.1.4 is published** (latest). Agents do not `npm publish`.

After a git clone, run `npm install && npm run build:mcp` in `examples/auspex-ts`, or MCP fail-closes with reason `DistMissing` (not an empty silent server). Published `npx -p auspex-solari auspex-mcp` includes `dist/`. Put `SOLARI_API_KEY` in the MCP `env`. Host paste cards: [docs/HOSTS.md](docs/HOSTS.md). Claude Code: [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md).

A login wait can run about 30 minutes. A tool timeout near 300 seconds ends first. Use `npx auspex-solari job`, then `job-status` (`auspex_job`, then `auspex_job_status`).

## Frozen door sequence

Seed/handoff door for off-site typing. Not a same-session VNC takeover.

1. Mint `login --url <https>` (derives `--profile` from the host; override `--profile <yours>`). Chooser is `handoff.url`. Phone: `handoff.mobileUrl`. Desktop: `handoff.desktopUrl`.
2. Human logs in. Secrets stay off agent chat, MCP, and receipts.
3. Human Save. Paste the copied line. The local field is cleared.
4. `await-login --save-editor`, then `finalize-login` only when the seed is the app session, not an IdP-only jar (`idp-only-save`, kind `app-visible`). Use `--url` and an expect unique to the logged-in app (absent from public marketing).
5. Later `check`. Optional `--verify-with-profile`.

New host: do not carry a previous `--profile`. A mismatch sets `profileHostMatch` false and `suggestedProfile`. Remint with that slug.

Many profiles: One profile per host. login --url names the slug (app.example.com → app-example-com). A different host gets its own profile. profiles lists them. Purge one name only after the human agrees (--purge <name> --yes).

## Clock

The typing window dies in about five minutes. A saved profile does not die with it. Detail: [docs/stream-jwt-solari.md](docs/stream-jwt-solari.md).
- While that window is still open, a dropped connection reconnects the same token. That is not `stream-expired`.
- After the window dies and the profile has no cookies, mint again.
- Human Save, then `await-login --save-editor`, then `finalize-login` only when the jar is the app session.
- `editorSave` 200 and the jar includes the app host but is not cookie-strong or local-storage-auth: finalize now, even if the window already died.
- App-origin cookies or allowlisted localStorage auth key names: `check --verify-with-profile`. `solariSaveReady` is not `claimOkProfile`. sessionStorage 0 is expected. Do not invent sessionStorage.
- The app is on screen and the jar is only Microsoft or Google cookies: do not finalize. Do not mint again to finish Microsoft.

## Long run

<!-- auspex-long-run:begin -->
A saved login can outlast the five-minute window. That span is the Solari profile and the site session, not an Auspex timer. There is no keepalive.

Before a long unattended loop, run `profile-status`, then on an auth-gated host `check --verify-with-profile` and read `claimOkProfile`. `ok`, `loggedIn`, `weakSeed`, and `app-visible` are not overnight-safe. The cadence is that pair, before the loop and again before an older pass. There is no minute timer.

Operator note: budget an occasional human door. Site expiry is the re-gate row. Longevity is the Solari profile and the site session, not an Auspex TTL. Operator page: docs/ops-runbook.md.

If you hit a sign-in wall, a fresh challenge, a dead typing window with no cookies, or a seed you cannot reuse: stop. One human door when the door table says `auspex_login`. Do not type a secret. Do not claim a CAPTCHA is solved. Do not keep checking for hours.

`app-visible` still means stop with no mint. `editorFold` `no-cdp` with the app host in the jar still means finalize now when that jar is not cookie-strong. A cookie-strong Save is check --verify-with-profile. solariSaveReady is not claimOkProfile.
<!-- auspex-long-run:end -->

## Schema v1 required keys

Check stdout is one JSON object. `schemaVersion` is `1`. Do not add required keys. Exit 0 only when `ok` is true.

- `schemaVersion` — `1`
- `ok` — agent success: `reason` is `matched`, and sandbox verify passed when it ran
- `reason` — `matched` | `loggedOut` | `needsHuman` | `mismatch` | `network` | `recordedLoggedIn` | `expectMatchedPublicLanding` | `hostChanged` | `stream-expired`
- `url` — requested URL, or landed URL if the request was empty
- `expect` — claim substring
- `screenshotPath` — on-disk PNG under `.auspex/runs/`

## If stuck

- The claim appeared on a public login or marketing page, so the profile was not saved (`expectMatchedPublicLanding`). Use the real app URL and text that only the logged-in app shows.
- The live site moved to a different host than the one minted into the door (`hostChanged`). Mint `auspex_login` again for `suggestedProfile` and `suggestedUrl`. Leave the old profile alone.
<!-- auspex-door-await:begin -->
- `idp-only-save` / `app-visible`: do not finalize. Do not mint again to finish Microsoft. The picture is not a saved login.
- `idp-only-save` / `sign-in-wall`: finish sign-in, land on the app UI, then Save, and mint again.
- `editorFold` `no-cdp` and the jar includes the app host: finalize-login now, even if the window already died. Skip `--verify-with-profile` on that fold.
- Bare `stream-expired` (no cookies): mint again. Skip a 30-minute wait. Do not treat this as finalize-now.
<!-- auspex-door-await:end -->
- `weakSeed` (counted in-tab session storage is 0): finalize-login while the token is live. This is not `app-visible`. Skip `--verify-with-profile`.
- `weakSeed` (stale folded session storage): mint again. This is not `app-visible`. Skip `--verify-with-profile`.
- `emptySave` (no saved profile): mint again. Do not finalize.
- `cookie-strong` or `local-storage-auth`: Solari Save already holds app-origin cookies or allowlisted localStorage auth key names. Counted sessionStorage 0 is expected. Run `check --verify-with-profile` and read `claimOkProfile`. `solariSaveReady` is not `claimOkProfile`. Do not finalize to invent sessionStorage. IdP hosts alone stay the IdP rows.
- Long unattended loop: [Long run](#long-run) and [docs/ops-runbook.md](docs/ops-runbook.md). Check the seed before you leave it. On a re-gate, stop.
- Solari returned HTTP 429 (too many browsers). Run `auspex_reap`, then retry. The HTTP list is in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#blame-solari-vs-auspex).
- Login mint is silent. Read `traceSummary` / `npx auspex-solari trace` before minting again.

## Do not

- Type a password or OTP, copy one into chat, or fill one from a vault or an agent.
- Build a Handraise-style same-session takeover. The door is off-site typing.
- Open Solari noVNC to fix the phone keyboard. Phone typing uses `handoff.mobileUrl`.
- Finalize because the dashboard is on screen (`idp-only-save` / `app-visible`).
- Call an Auspex remote HTTP server. Local stdio only.
- Turn on CAPTCHA, stealth, or a proxy. Leave them alone.
- Install npm `auspex` or run `npm publish`. The package is `auspex-solari`.
- SOLARI_API_KEY is env-only. Never commit .auspex/, .env, or keys.
- `--record` a logged-in session, or run `auspex_verify` after a default check.
- Treat `ok` as `claimOk` or `claimOkProfile`. Do not fold `claimOkProfile` into `ok`.
- Treat `solariSaveReady` as `claimOkProfile`. A cookie or localStorage Save still needs `check --verify-with-profile`.
- Treat `loggedIn`, `weakSeed`, or `app-visible` as safe for an unattended 24–48h loop, or invent a keepalive. Longevity is the Solari profile and the site session.
